title: Squeezed- and coherent-state quantum key distribution over a deployed hybrid fibre-free-space channel
authors: Dnan A. E. Hajomer, Huy Q. Nguyen, Ivan Derkach, Andreas B. Kidmose, Edoardo Rossi, Mattia Sabatini, Yoann Pietri, Marco Avesani, Francesco Vedovato, Michael Hentschel, Radim Filip, Giuseppe Vallone, Vladyslav Usenko, Tobias Gehring, Soren Forchhammer, Paolo Villoresi, Ulrik L. Andersen
abstract: Quantum networks will combine optical fibre with free-space links, yet continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) has been developed predominantly for one medium or the other, while operation across concatenated fibre-free-space channels remains largely unexplored. The two media impose contrasting requirements: fibre transmission is stable and permits long processing intervals, whereas atmospheric propagation imposes transmittance fluctuations that degrade security and must be resolved on short timescales. Here we demonstrate a locally generated local oscillator CV-QKD with both Gaussian-modulated coherent and squeezed states over a deployed hybrid channel comprising a 620-m free-space link and 2 km of deployed fibre, with a total loss up to 20 dB. Rather than adapting the optics to each medium, we move channel adaptation to the post-processing, through a unified adaptive post-processing framework coupling transmittance-based clustering, residual-fading mitigation by covariance-matrix averaging or de-fading, and rate-adaptive blind reconciliation, which alone recovers up to 19% additional key. The same adaptive-processing principle is applied to both protocols, while accounting for their different security analyses and statistical requirements, yielding asymptotic secret-key rates of 0.42 Mbit per sec for the coherent-state protocol and 0.93 Mbit per sec for the squeezed-state protocol under the respective channel conditions, and establishing squeezed-state CV-QKD over a deployed atmospheric channel. These results show that adaptation to the transmission medium can largely be transferred to the data-processing layer, providing a route towards heterogeneous quantum networks spanning fibre, terrestrial free-space and satellite links.
summary: This paper demonstrates CV-QKD over a realistic hybrid channel combining optical fibre and free-space links. The key innovation is a unified adaptive post-processing framework that manages channel fluctuations by adapting the data processing rather than the optics. This successfully establishes high secret-key rates, paving the way for heterogeneous quantum networks.
main_problem: Demonstrating Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution (CV-QKD) over a complex, deployed hybrid channel combining optical fibre and free-space links, which requires handling contrasting channel requirements.
main_result: The authors achieved asymptotic secret-key rates of 0.42 Mbit/s (coherent) and 0.93 Mbit/s (squeezed) by developing a unified adaptive post-processing framework.
method: The core methodology involves applying an adaptive post-processing framework that couples transmittance-based clustering, residual-fading mitigation (de-fading), and rate-adaptive blind reconciliation.
model_or_system: The experiment uses a locally generated local oscillator (LLO) CV-QKD setup transmitting both Gaussian-modulated coherent and squeezed states over a hybrid link comprising 2 km of deployed fibre and a 620-m free-space atmospheric link.
key_observables: Asymptotic secret-key rates (Mbit/s), key lengths (bits), and the channel transmittance ($\eta$) and excess noise ($\epsilon$).
important_parameters: Total loss up to 20 dB; the contrast between stable fibre transmission and fluctuating atmospheric propagation.
main_assumptions: The security analysis relies on Gaussian extremality applied to the covariance matrix in fading channels, and the authors treat detector efficiency and electronic noise as trusted.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the experimental setup for the hybrid CV-QKD system in Padova, detailing components for both coherent and squeezed state transmission across the free-space and fibre segments.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of hybrid channel QKD, details the use of LLO schemes with coherent and squeezed states, and focuses heavily on the development and validation of the unified adaptive post-processing framework to extract key rates.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the practical implementation of quantum networks by solving the complex engineering challenge of integrating disparate physical media (fiber/free-space) into a single, functional quantum communication link.

Figure 1 presents the CV-QKD system and the hybrid fibre–free- space testbed deployed in Padova, Italy [24, 25]. The system im- plements both the Gaussian-modulated coherent- and squeezed- state protocols using a LLO scheme. The two protocols share the same modulation, synchronisation and digital signal processing (DSP), and differ in the quantum-state source, the detection front end, and the security analysis applied to the recovered data. Op- erating both over the same deployed link therefore exercises the adaptive post-processing framework on two protocols with different statistical requirements, using a common transmitter and DSP chain.
